design.text: Randomized, open-label, controlled trial; 350 patients randomized 1:1 to tivozanib 1.34 mg once daily for 21 consecutive days followed by 7 days off vs. sorafenib 400 mg twice daily; stratified by IMDC risk category and prior therapy.

citations.quote: In a Phase 3 trial, TIVO-3, 350 patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to tivozanib at a dose of 1.34 mg once daily for 21 consecutive days followed by 7 days off or to sorafenib 400 mg twice daily.
Randomization was stratified by International Metastatic RCC Database Consortium (IMDC) risk category and prior therapy

population.text: Adult patients with relapsed or refractory advanced RCC who received 2 or 3 prior systemic treatments (2 TKIs, a TKI plus a checkpoint inhibitor, or a TKI plus other agent), ECOG PS ≤1.

citations.quote: The primary evidence of efficacy and safety is provided by a pivotal randomized, open-label, controlled trial (TIVO-3) in patients with relapsed or refractory advanced RCC, who received prior systemic treatments (2 TKIs, a TKI plus a checkpoint inhibitor or a TKI plus other agent).
To be eligible, patients were required to have had previous treatment with 2 prior lines of systemic therapy and to have an ECOG PS \le1.

endpoint.text: Progression-free survival (PFS) in all randomized patients per Blinded Independent Review Committee (BIRC) assessment.

citations.quote: The major efficacy outcome measure was progression free survival (PFS) in all randomized patients per Blinded Independent Review Committee (BIRC) review of imaging.

In a Phase 3 trial, TIVO-3, 350 patients with advanced renal cell carcinoma were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to tivozanib at a dose of 1.34 mg once daily for 21 consecutive days followed by 7 days off or to sorafenib 400 mg twice daily.
A statistically significant improvement in PFS was observed for patients randomized to tivozanib (n=175) vs. sorafenib (n=175).

result.text: PFS HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.56 to 0.95), p=0.016; median PFS 5.59 months (tivozanib) vs. 3.88 months (sorafenib). ORR 18% vs. 8%. Final OS HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.75 to 1.24); median OS 16.39 vs. 19.15 months.

citations.quote: The estimate of the hazard ratio (HR) for PFS was 0.73 (95% CI: 0.56 to 0.95, p-value of 0.016).
Median PFS estimate was 5.59 months (95% CI: 4.83, 7.33) in the tivozanib
arm vs. 3.88 months (95% CI: 3.71 to 5.55) in the sorafenib arm.

The objective response rate (ORR) was 18% (95% CI: 12%, 24%) in the tivozanib arm vs. 8% (95% CI: 4%, 13%) in the sorafenib arm; these results were supportive of the overall efficacy of tivozanib vs. sorafenib.
The final median overall survival (OS) estimate was 16.39 months for the tivozanib arm vs. 19.15 months for the sorafenib arm; however, the HR was 0.97 (95% CI: 0.75 to 1.24).

indication.text: FOTIVDA is indicated for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory advanced renal cell carcinoma (RCC) following two or more prior systemic therapies.

target_moa.text: Tivozanib is a kinase inhibitor that inhibits phosphorylation of VEGFR-1, VEGFR-2 and VEGFR-3, and also inhibits other kinases including c-kit and PDGFRβ at clinically relevant concentrations.

citations.quote: Tivozanib is a kinase inhibitor (KI) that inhibits phosphorylation of vascular endothelial growth factor receptor (VEGFR) 1, VEGFR 2 and VEGFR 3 and inhibits other kinases including c-kit and PDGFR \beta at clinically relevant concentrations, as demonstrated via in vitro cellular kinase assays.
Tivozanib hydrochloride is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor of vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGFR)-1, -2, and -3.

key_safety.text: Most common (≥20%) adverse reactions: fatigue, hypertension, diarrhea, decreased appetite, nausea, dysphonia, hypothyroidism, cough, and stomatitis. Serious adverse reactions occurred in 45% of FOTIVDA patients; fatal adverse reactions in 8% (including pneumonia 1.7%). Hypertension occurred in 45% (22% ≥Grade 3). Hemorrhagic events in 11%.

basis.text: The prior CR letter (June 6, 2013) was based on review of TIVO-1, which showed a trend towards a detrimental effect on overall survival with tivozanib in treatment-naïve advanced RCC.

citations.quote: Although TIVO-1 met its primary endpoint (PFS HR = 0.80 [95% CI: 0.64, 0.99], p = 0.04), a trend towards a detrimental effect on survival was observed with tivozanib (OS HR = 1.25 [95% CI: 0.95, 1.62], p = 0.11).

summary.text: NDA 212904 for tivozanib was submitted and received March 31, 2020 under standard review, with a PDUFA goal date of March 31, 2021, and received regular (not accelerated) approval based on the PFS benefit in the pivotal Phase 3 TIVO-3 trial.
